rows.title: Applied AI Engineer - Remote
rows.comp: Not disclosed — "Fair compensation based on skills, experience, and location"
rows.why: The requirement list is unusually close to what he actually does: LLM-based workflows and AI-powered product features, plus "serious experience using AI development tools — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot", which is his daily toolchain rather than a nice-to-have. It also states it weighs "high-agency" capability over formal seniority, which is the framing that lets ~3 years and no CS degree through.
rows.watch_outs: Language: "Clear written and spoken English" is the stated requirement; German is listed only as a nice-to-have, so this is genuinely an English-language role — but the German nice-to-have signals a DACH-anchored team. Location is given only as "Remote" with no country or region eligibility sentence, so confirm Italy is in scope before investing. Python is the must-have backend language, not TypeScript.

rows.title: Senior Software Engineer - Frontend
rows.location: Milan, Italy (hybrid, min 2 days/week in office)
rows.why: React frontend on embedded UIs and financial dashboards maps onto his Bubble.io-to-Next.js migration and the FlowSpace product work that took the platform from 2,000 to 4,500+ users. Milan is a train ride from Venice, the band is disclosed, and it is the freshest genuinely English-language Italian engineering role found in the sweep.
rows.watch_outs: Language: "Fluency in English is essential (most stakeholders are UK-based)" and Italian is listed only as nice-to-have — the cleanest English-language statement of any Italian posting checked. Asks 5+ years professional frontend engineering against his ~3, so lead-level scope is what he has to sell. Hybrid means 2 days/week on site in Milan, not remote-within-Italy. No AI or automation surface in the role.

rows.title: Agentic AI Engineer (m/f/d)
rows.posted: not stated on the posting (SmartRecruiters shows no date)
rows.why: Squarely Track A: agentic systems on Python with OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, LangChain and LLMOps, which is the production-agent work he already ships (support agents, scraping/parsing tools, the n8n + Eden AI CV parser). No year count is stated, so his ~3 years is not screened out at the door.
rows.watch_outs: Language: "You communicate fluently in English and appreciate cultural diversity" — English is the stated requirement and Portuguese is not mentioned anywhere. But it is an on-site Lisbon role, so Tier 3: an intra-EU move plus a new residence registration, not a remote option. SIXT is a large corporate with a long hiring loop, no comp disclosed, and no posted date visible — check the age before applying. Java or Go also listed alongside Python.

rows.title: Senior Software Engineer - Backend
rows.location: Milan, Italy (hybrid, min 2 days/week in office)
rows.why: Partner integrations across microservices is the same shape of work as his Office RnD, Nexudus, Sendgrid, Clubee and CRM lead-capture integrations, and the JD explicitly wants engineers using "agentic AI tools to accelerate daily development" — a rare Italian posting that treats his AI tooling as an asset rather than a curiosity.
rows.watch_outs: Language: "Fluency in English is essential (most stakeholders are UK-based)", Italian nice-to-have only. 5+ years asked against his ~3. Backend stack leans microservices/event-streaming with Scala preferred on the adjacent Software Engineer II req, so his Laravel/Node background is adjacent rather than matching. Hybrid Milan, 2 days/week on site.

rows.title: Senior Forward Deployed Engineer
rows.location: Lisbon, Portugal (hybrid; posting also covers Porto)
rows.why: Embedded enterprise engagements turning "AI ambition into working capability" is the forward-deployed pitch he is strongest on — he has done exactly this across eight European companies, mediating between internal teams and an external agency and owning business-logic documentation. Track B converts best for him and the company runs the same role in Munich and London, so the practice is real, not a single-client staffing bet.
rows.watch_outs: Language: the posting states no language requirement at all — Portuguese is not asked for, but neither is English confirmed in writing, so treat "English is fine" as an inference from the English-only JD across three countries rather than a stated fact. On-site/hybrid Lisbon means Tier 3 relocation. Published 2026-03-06, five months stale — confirm it is still being actively recruited. "Senior" in the title with no year count stated.

rows.title: Product Manager, AI & Content Operations
rows.why: An AI-and-content-operations PM role at an Italian company that will take a remote-within-Italy hire is the rare Track D listing where his mix fits: business-logic documentation, QA, coordinating an external agency, and shipped AI pipelines rather than PM theory. No permit friction and he can be in Bologna in two hours.
rows.watch_outs: Language: English is the emphasised working requirement and Italian is explicitly only "a plus" — one of the few Italian postings that says so. The real problem is age: the Lever API reports createdAt around February 2025, roughly 18 months ago, so although it is still listed and live on the board it may be a long-idle req. Worth a direct note to the recruiter before writing a full application. No comp disclosed.

rows.title: Software Engineer, Backend - Business Domain
rows.location: Milan, Italy (hybrid, 3 days/week in office: Tue, Thu + 1 of choice)
rows.why: One of the few Italian scale-ups that states outright it does not need Italian, and it asks for exactly 3 years of industry experience — his number. The work is backend systems for fee calculation, invoicing, payout orchestration and settlement flows, which is business-logic ownership of the kind he did at FlowSpace.
rows.watch_outs: Language: "You are fluent in English, both written and spoken" — Italian is not required, verified in the posting body. The gate is the stack: Java is the primary language and he has shipped none of it, so this is the weakest stack overlap on the list. Also 3 days/week on site in Milan (heavier than Moneyfarm's 2), published 2026-01-07 so seven months old, and no comp disclosed. Only apply if he is willing to argue transferable backend skills into a Java team.
